can_do: Can use the past perfect continuous talk about a background action or event which began before a point in the past and was still continuing up to a point in the past when the main event happened.

Once I had been watching TV for 6 hours when my Mum suddenly switched it off. (Russia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Russian; Pass)

can_do: Can use the past perfect continuous after a time conjunction to give background information.
examples: After we had been sunbathing at the beach all day long, we went every evening to a cosy restaurant called "The Barking Cat", where we had a good meal and some wine. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)
After I had been waiting for an hour, I decided to go through the gate and go in on foot. (Italy; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Italian; Pass)

can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
examples: I had been working on the project for over a year. (France; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; French; Pass)
We had been waiting for hours. (Greece; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Greek; Pass)
I didn't need so much, because I'd been saving money for a few months. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; Spanish - European; Pass)

guideword: FORM/USE: BACKGROUND INFORMATION WITH RELATIVE CLAUSE
can_do: Can use the past perfect continuous in a relative clause to give background information.  ► relative clauses
examples: And there were two men who had been chasing the murderer to find out who the man is and rescue the girl.... (Korea, North; B2 VANTAGE; 2008; Korean; Pass)
The guide also tells some funny stories about an old lord, who had been living there in the 18th century. (Germany; B2 VANTAGE; 2001; German; Pass)
After a few minutes the door was opened and the man who  had been following me came in. (Spain; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Spanish - European; Pass)

guideword: FORM/USE: WITH 'BY' IN A RELATIVE CLAUSE|

I bought a T-shirt, it cost £42 because it is made of cotton. (Argentina; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

can_do: Can use the passive with 'by' to add information about something already known.
examples: It was bought by my uncle. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Chinese; Pass)
It's made by Sony-Ericsson, I love it … (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Italian; Pass)
… it was written by an excellent author, Lev Tolstoy. (Russia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Russian; Pass)

can_do: Can use the present simple passive affirmative with a range of pronoun and noun subjects.
examples: Our office is situated near the airport. (B1 Argentina ; Spanish - Latin American)
The walls are painted in a dark blue, and the floor is wood. (B1 Dutch)

can_do: Can use the past simple passive affirmative with a range of pronoun and noun subjects both singular and plural.
examples: It was written in a strange language that I tried to translate. (B1 Spanish - Latin American)
Next day, I heard that my neighbour's car was stolen. (B1 Polish)
They filmed the flowers and trees, and some pupils were interviewed about their work in the garden, too. (B1 German)

can_do: Can use the present continuous passive affirmative with a limited range of verbs.
examples: Did you know that the next Harry Potter movie is being filmed in my school? (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Catalan; Pass)
Why don't we stay at my house and visit Tokyo, where an interesting Japanese history exhibition is being held. (Japan; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Japanese; Pass)
As a result of that, Russia's economy is being followed by many experts. (Turkey; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Turkish; Pass)
They filmed a class where the clothes are being tested at the moment and they interviewed some people. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; German; Pass)

can_do: Can use the passive infinitive after a limited number of forms including 'going to', 'have to', 'need to', 'want to'.
examples: It is going to be shown this Friday. (B1 PET Turkish)
After that, they printed an authorisation, form which had to be signed by my parents because I'm not over eighteen. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)
He wants to be informed about sales development by the end of November 2001. (B1 Switzerland German)

can_do: Can use the passive infinitive affirmative and negative forms after an increasing range of main verbs, modal verbs, adjectives and nouns, in impersonal constructions.
examples: According to your advertisement, some training is supposed to be given. (B2 South Korean)
My composition was ready to be printed and I was searching for a piece of paper… (B2 Austria)
I would prefer to sleep in a tent because I have never done it and I think it is an experience not to be missed, a very original adventure! (B2 French)
The reason that I took part in your research was to help youngsters not to be addicted to computer games …  (B2 Greek)
For one, the future homes might not be built out of bricks at all! (Korea, South; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; Korean; Pass)

can_do: Can use the present continuous passive to refer to the future.
examples: The seminar is being held at Chennai in the next week. (India; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Marathi; Pass)
We are being visited by our Sales Director on Thursday morning. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; Portuguese; Pass)

can_do: Can use the past perfect passive affirmative form.
examples: The car had been serviced and everything seemed to be all right. (B2 Portuguese)
At this moment, Lime walked in and realised he had been set up. (B2 Dutch)

can_do: Can use the passive with 'by' to give focus.
examples: My school was chosen by the TV company because it is one of the newest in town. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

guideword: FORM: WITH VERBS TAKING TWO OBJECTS.
can_do: Can use the past simple passive with a limited range of verbs needing two objects, putting the indirect object in subject position.
examples: So I was given a ticket for a train, running from Berlin to Munich. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; German; Pass)
We were lucky, because we were given another chance. (Yugoslavia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Serbian; Pass)

can_do: Can use the present simple passive negative with a range of pronoun and noun subjects.
examples: The story is about a girl, who is not accepted in her class. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; German; Pass)
I think we should replace the printer, because it prints very slowly and the sheets aren't printed properly. (Switzerland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Swiss German; Pass)

can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
examples: You can see a lot of special places in Wroclaw. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH, 2007, Polish)
You can make a quick snack, for example, a sandwich. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH, 2006, German)

can_do: Can use the affirmative question form.
examples: Can you come for dinner Monday at 6.00 pm? (Arabic - Other, A1 BREAKTHROUGH, Pass, 2008)

can_do: Can use the negative forms.
examples: I cannot come to see you. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH, 2009, Bengali)
I'm very nervous and I can't say anything. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH Polish)

can_do: Can use 'could' to make requests.
examples: Could you help me to paint my bedroom? (Portuguese, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2006)
I left my umbrella in your house yesterday. … Could you bring it to school tomorrow, please? (Czech, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2005)

can_do: Can use the negative form of 'could' to talk about inability.
examples: [talking about the key to an office] I couldn't work without it. (Germany; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; German; Pass)
I couldn't buy the T-shirt because it was too expensive, but the other things were very nice and quite cheap, so I bought them. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
examples: You could come by bus, and we could meet at the bus station. (Spanish - European, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2010)
We could go to the museum near Cibeles. (Spanish - European, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2001)

can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
examples: [talking about clothes] So I may need them. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Gujarati; Pass)
I think it may be dirty. (Thailand; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Thai; Pass)

can_do: Can use 'may' to talk about weak possibility referring to the present and the future.
examples: [talking about an important document] It may be in our room inside my bag. (Assamese, A2 WAYSTAGE)
… bring some money with you. We may need it. (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Portuguese; Pass)
[talking about buying clothes for the summer] And the weather may be hot. (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; French; Pass)

can_do: Can use 'may' with a limited range of adverbs (most commonly 'also') in the normal mid-position after the modal verb. ► adverbs
examples: I may also ask you for another favour.... (India; B1 THRESHOLD; 2005; Hindi; Fail)
Why don't you try going to the gym before work? It may also help you release stress? (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
examples: The weather might be hot and sunny. (Spanish - Latin American, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2009)
I think it might be in your bedroom. (Portuguese, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2005)

can_do: Can use 'might' to make polite suggestions and give advice.
examples: The park is a great place for picnic. It has lots of trees, a beautiful view and fresh air. You might need to bring some food and drink. (Turkish, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2009)
I really don't know what you should do, but I think that you might talk with your parents. (Italian, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2008)

can_do: Can use 'might have' + '-ed' to talk about possibility with a past reference.

I thought that a burglar might have broken into our house. (Turkey; B2 VANTAGE; 2001; Turkish; Pass)

can_do: Can use the negative forms.
examples: … you mustn't forget to buy some strawberry juice for us. (Portuguese, A2 WAYSTAGE)
You must not wear a white colour shirt, you can only wear a dark colour shirt. (Chinese, A2 WAYSTAGE)

can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
examples: You must wear your sports shoes and you must also bring your racket! (Greek)
I must be back at 10.15. (French)

can_do: Can use 'must' to make invitations.
examples: You must come and stay in our house too. (Turkey; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Turkish; Pass)
You must come and see this restaurant! (Switzerland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2005; Swiss German; Pass)

can_do: Can use 'shall I' to make offers.
examples: Shall I go and buy some cake and crackers? (Bulgarian, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2009)
The tickets cost €25. Shall I buy you one? (Spanish - European, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2010)

can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
examples: We shall start tomorrow at 2 o'clock. (Marathi, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2006)
I shall be free on Sunday at 6 o'clock in the evening. (Ukraine; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Russian; Pass)

can_do: Can use 'shall' with 'we' to make suggestions.

can_do: Can use the negative form.
examples: You shouldn't miss it. (Thai, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2007)
It is a new flat, so there shouldn't be any problems. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Polish; Fail)
I think you should not wear your favourite clothes because they may get dirty. (Thai, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2006)

can_do: Can use the affirmative form.

We should buy 2 tickets. (Chinese, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2010)

can_do: Can use the question form.

can_do: Can use 'will' to ask about plans and intentions.

can_do: Can use 'would like to invite' to make invitations.

When can we meet? (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Spanish - European; Pass)

How  do you feel? (Thailand; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Thai; Pass)
